opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
What exactly was the covenant with Abraham?
In the Book of Genesis (especially chapters 12, 15, and 17), God makes a covenant—a binding, relational promise—with Abraham. It has a few key parts:
God’s promises: *Descendants: Abraham will become “a father of a multitude of nations” *Land: The land of Canaan is given to his descendants *Blessings: Through Abraham, all nations will be blessed.
Abraham’s part: Faith and trust in God, obedience to God’s will; the outward sign: circumcision (a physical mark of belonging to the covenant). So the covenant isn’t just a contract—it’s a relationship:
“I will be your God, and you will be my people.”

The psalmist states: “Look to the Lord… seek to serve Him constantly”.  That line (from Psalm 105) reflects how to live inside that covenant: Remember what God has done, Stay faithful, Seek Him continually, not just occasionally. It’s basically the response God asks for: an ongoing relationship, not just belief.

In the Gospel of John 8:51–59, things escalate dramatically. When Jesus says:
“Before Abraham was, "I AM”
He’s not just saying He existed earlier—He’s invoking the divine name revealed to Moses in the Book of Exodus (“I AM WHO AM”). Why this caused outrage: The listeners understand this as a claim to divinity. That’s why they accuse Him of blasphemy and try to stone Him.  Why does Jesus say they don’t know God? They believe they know God because they follow the laws, and they are descendants of Abraham. But Jesus is saying: If you truly knew God, you would recognize Me. So the issue isn’t knowledge about God—it’s recognition of God’s presence when He shows up.  Jesus said, “Abraham rejoiced to see my day”
This line is powerful.
Jesus is saying: Abraham’s faith wasn’t just about land (that he did not have) or descendants (he clearly did not live to see), It was ultimately pointing forward to God’s fulfillment—through Christ.  Abraham trusted God without seeing the full picture.  Those in front of Jesus see the fulfillment but reject it.  

The big connection across all three readings:
Abraham: trusts God → enters covenant
Psalms-->calls people to remain faithful to that covenant.

Jesus: reveals Himself as the fulfillment of that covenant.  But the tension seen in the Gospel is, the same God is present—but not everyone recognizes Him.  

The line that struck me —“seek to serve Him constantly”—becomes the key.
Because it is not enough to inherit faith (like being Abraham’s descendant).  It’s about actively seeking God, and being open enough to recognizing Him—even when He comes in unexpected ways
